capabilities.title: Project composition and architectural boundaries
capabilities.description: Supporting infrastructure for the Godot/.NET project, shared event contracts, composition, and protected layer boundaries.
capabilities.boundary_rationale: Contains environment and structural enforcement work; domain contracts are grouped with their gameplay responsibilities.

capabilities.title: Deterministic outcome generation and locking
capabilities.description: Shared RNG state, offer provenance, immutable offers, and preservation across re-entry or resume.
capabilities.boundary_rationale: Covers explicit outcome locking and shared random-state responsibilities; deterministic combat arithmetic remains with combat rules.

capabilities.title: Card identity and deck lifecycle
capabilities.description: Card forms, instances, curse constraints, shared deck operations, and live pile state.
capabilities.boundary_rationale: Tracks the card/deck model and its runtime bindings; reward acquisition and card-play execution have their own groupings.

capabilities.title: Combat interaction and runtime orchestration
capabilities.description: Validated card play, turn sequencing, scene bindings, targeting, hooks, completion, and player feedback.
capabilities.boundary_rationale: The shared combat execution path and interaction shell; enemy behavior, status arithmetic, and deck management remain separately navigable.

capabilities.title: Status, modifiers, and damage resolution
capabilities.description: Status contracts and lifecycle, deterministic triggers, fixed damage, AOE, multi-hit rules, and faithful visible results.
capabilities.boundary_rationale: Groups resolution semantics with their live promotion and display; generic combat hooks and action orchestration belong to CAP-COMBAT-INTERACTION-AND-RUNTIME-ORCHESTRATION.

capabilities.title: Enemy definitions, intent, and action execution
capabilities.description: Data-backed enemies, intent selection and preview, action resolution, no-repeat rules, and structured timed effects.
capabilities.boundary_rationale: The enemy behavior chain from definition to visible action; player targeting is owned by combat interaction.

capabilities.title: Warrior playable identity
capabilities.description: Warrior selection, starting cards, combat seeding, and Rage integration.
capabilities.boundary_rationale: A character-specific vertical slice limited to the explicitly supplied Warrior scope.

capabilities.title: Run entry and difficulty
capabilities.description: Main menu, selection flow, immutable difficulty, rule modifiers, and difficulty visibility.
capabilities.boundary_rationale: Player run setup and difficulty semantics; continuation storage and restoration remain in CAP-SAVE-INTEGRITY-AND-CONTINUE-RECOVERY.

capabilities.title: Act maps and route ownership
capabilities.description: Modular Act data, generated route graphs, legal node selection, run transitions, and owned entry/return paths.
capabilities.boundary_rationale: Run navigation and route state; individual node transactions are separately grouped, with explicit route work cross-listed.

capabilities.title: Reward offers and acquisition
capabilities.description: Contextual drop pools, three-choice offers, selection, confirmation, skipping, fallback, and reward-entry modification.
capabilities.boundary_rationale: Reward transaction lifecycle; shared outcome locking is cross-listed in CAP-DETERMINISTIC-OUTCOME-GENERATION-AND-LOCKING and broader relic execution remains in CAP-RELICS-AND-EFFECTFUL-COMBAT-PARTICIPANTS.

capabilities.title: Shop, rest, and event services
capabilities.description: Noncombat node choices, costs, purchases, card services, healing, upgrades, removal, and player-visible results.
capabilities.boundary_rationale: Cohesion is noncombat node transactions and their route integration; reward choice is a separately developed transaction lifecycle.

capabilities.title: Relics and effectful combat participants
capabilities.description: Relic contracts and catalog, acquisition/equip/display, combat and run effects, powers, and potions.
capabilities.boundary_rationale: Persistent relic ownership and effects plus explicitly related participant surfaces; generic hook infrastructure is CAP-COMBAT-INTERACTION-AND-RUNTIME-ORCHESTRATION.

capabilities.title: Save integrity and Continue recovery
capabilities.description: Atomic saves, autosave boundaries, integrity/migration gates, blocked-state UX, and restored run surfaces.
capabilities.boundary_rationale: Persistence and recovery behavior including dedicated determinism tests; summary-only evidence display belongs to CAP-RUN-SUMMARY-AND-SETTLEMENT.

capabilities.title: Run summary and settlement
capabilities.description: Stored-data presentation of outcome, difficulty, route progress, reward/relic results, and resume evidence.
capabilities.boundary_rationale: Reporting stored run results without recomputation; does not own reward execution or save restoration.

capabilities.title: Localization and accessible interaction
capabilities.description: Translation infrastructure and content, rendered-text validation, focus cycles, and accessible input fallback.
capabilities.boundary_rationale: Cross-scene usability support; ordinary visual feedback stays with its gameplay surface unless localization or accessibility is explicit.

capabilities.title: Automated quality gates and verification
capabilities.description: Headless smoke execution, suite aggregation, coverage controls, audit validation, traceability, and boundary checks.
capabilities.boundary_rationale: Supporting verification mechanisms and explicit domain tests; review-scope policy is CAP-TASK-SCOPE-AND-REVIEW-GOVERNANCE and runtime security enforcement is CAP-SECURITY-CONTROLS-AND-AUDIT-EVIDENCE.

capabilities.title: Security controls and audit evidence
capabilities.description: Determinism/security JSONL evidence, guarded process execution, and security-sensitive signal validation.
capabilities.boundary_rationale: Host-facing enforcement and audit contracts; test-pipeline integrations overlap CAP-AUTOMATED-QUALITY-GATES-AND-VERIFICATION only where explicitly stated.

capabilities.title: Task scope and review governance
capabilities.description: Bounded semantic review, deterministic closure sizing, integration checkpoints, and separated review lanes.
capabilities.boundary_rationale: Governance rather than new gameplay delivery; review splits are kept here rather than counted as runtime implementation.

per_task_analysis.rationale: Pins Godot 4.5.1 .NET and .NET 8 setup and requires the package lock file.
Establishes Core, Godot, and test directory boundaries and NewRouge namespaces.
Defines card identity, Base/U1A/U1B/Ultimate forms, and upgrade fields.
Defines shared offer-lock structure, provenance, and RNG stream contracts.
Defines Buff, Debuff, and RuleModifier contracts with deterministic ordering.
Combat phases and sequencing define orchestration; the same contract explicitly covers damage calculation rules.
Provides the shared event bus and the canonical contracts location.
Implements card definitions, instances, and transitions between forms.
Provides the deterministic RNG stream registry and state management.
Implements status application, stacking, decay, and dispel boundaries.
Implements the core validated card-play resolution pipeline.
Implements save serialization, schema versioning, and atomic writes.
Configures Godot autoloads and dependency composition.
Creates New Run and Quit entry actions and explicitly exposes single-slot Continue.
Provides selection and descriptions for ten difficulty levels.
Creates the character selection step and restricts playable selection and mechanism summary to Warrior.
Makes Act structure modular rather than fixing the map to three Acts.
Creates the combat UI shell and binds it to core combat state.
Creates three-card reward choice and explicitly locks offers for deterministic display.
Creates purchasable shop inventory with no upgrade service and explicitly locks that inventory.
Creates the rest choice surface with a free card upgrade option.
Creates event choices with explicit HP-loss and curse-card cost examples.
Sets up translation resources and key naming conventions.
Defines the Warrior-specific ten-card starting deck, supplying card/deck content.
Defines Warrior Rage as a combat-only state buff integrated with statuses.
Defines the immutable run-level difficulty contract with values 1-10.
Translates selected difficulty into rule modifiers, including the stated OverplayTax threshold example.
Defines ActConfig and JSON loading for modular Act data.
Defines Act- and encounter-specific card drop pools with rarity tiers.
Defines relic definition and instance contracts.
Provides twenty unique relic definitions with hookable effects.
Defines non-upgradable curse cards and the removal services that operate on them.
Implements shared deterministic draw, discard, exhaust, and retain operations with hand limit ten.
Adds hover and drag targeting to the combat interaction path.
Resolves victory/defeat and explicitly hands completed combat to rewards.
Triggers autosaves at combat start, reward opening, and event choice.
Adds single-slot run metadata, integrity checks, and Continue gating.
Writes JSONL audit evidence for security events and explicitly for determinism events.
Populates translations for M1 cards, relics, events, and UI text.
Defines Act 1 encounter enemy data.
Displays each enemy's next intent on the combat surface.
Locks node selection and prevents map backtracking.
Restricts run-state transitions to Command entries.
Adds headless GdUnit4 integration tests, verifying save/resume behavior and deterministic reward/shop/event outcomes.
Exposes selected difficulty in the HUD and explicitly in the run summary.
Generates and locks offer candidates using RNG streams and provenance.
Implements deterministic status trigger ordering and fixed damage behavior.
Implements damage calculation with AOE and multi-hit resolution order.
Adds combat-loop stability limits of 100 cards per turn and failure handling.
Validates save migration and blocks Continue when saves are invalid.
Connects combat turn flow to core services and explicitly wires persistence save points.
Implements deterministic enemy intent selection rules.
Adds the Windows Python headless smoke runner and strict success-marker validation.
Aggregates selected GdUnit4 suites into hard/soft quality gates and summary JSON.
Implements configurable xUnit coverage thresholds and hard/soft gate modes.
Validates security audit JSONL and explicitly integrates that validator with quality gates.
Adds the dedicated ADR/chapter/overlay Test-Refs traceability gate.
Bounds semantic soft review to task scope and preserves deterministic hard-gate precedence.
Wires menu, difficulty, and character selection into the real Map entry route.
Owns Map entry into Combat/Event/Shop/Rest and completed-node return routing.
Creates the standalone Reward scene and owns Combat/Event-to-Reward-to-Map routes.
Creates the rest service surface for healing/upgrades/removal and explicitly owns Map entry/return.
Makes Continue blocking reasons and recovery options visible to the player.
Shows combat action results, invalid commands, and decision-critical HUD state.
Validates translation-key usage and nonempty, non-key-echo text across supported locales.
Owns the run summary surface for stored outcome, difficulty, progress, and recovery metadata.
Binds shop purchase/remove/transform/leave behavior and explicitly owns its route without upgrade services.
Provides focus-cycle and accessibility work across M1 player-facing surfaces.
Makes event costs, choices, results, and blocks visible and owns feedback return-to-Map routing.
Adds connected legal edges, locked paths, completed history, and reachable choices on existing route ownership.
Tracks deck lifecycle integration over T80-T82 as an umbrella checkpoint, explicitly avoiding a separate implementation track.
Binds existing card definitions and localized text to CombatScene costs, targeting rules, and effect resolution.
Extends legal combat targeting to multiple living enemies while retaining existing victory-route ownership.
Adds drag/hover/release/cancel and invalid-target feedback while explicitly retaining accessible click/button fallback.
Exposes existing player/enemy status semantics as visible combat state with deterministic updates.
Binds data-driven intent generation and previews, explicitly deferring action resolution and no-repeat rules.
Registers deterministic combat hooks for card play, turns, damage, and death checks; participant effects remain deferred.
Adds combat presentation feedback without mutating deterministic runtime, routing, or RNG ownership.
Unifies HP updates so any HP<=0 transition resolves defeat exactly once.
Replaces scene-local counters with shared DeckService draw/play/discard/end-turn state.
Exposes the shared draw-empty reshuffle cycle with discard reset before continued draws.
Displays total deck count and draw+hand+discard invariance over the shared deck runtime.
Hands scene card resolution to CombatService/PlayCard while explicitly deferring Warrior deck seeding and Rage.
Generates the initial three-card reward from existing pools using current Act and encounter context.
Makes one reward selectable and gates confirmation on that selection.
Generates route graphs from ActConfig while deferring Map surface binding.
Restores autosaves at real Map/combat entry boundaries, connecting Continue recovery to run navigation.
Promotes relic acquisition, equipped state, and visible run ownership while deferring combat effects.
Instantiates runtime combat enemies from existing enemy definitions.
Promotes trigger ordering and fixed damage into live combat while deferring AOE and feedback closure.
Builds a stored-data settlement surface for outcome and route progress, deferring later metadata additions.
Uses xUnit architecture tests to enforce Core/Godot separation and adapter-only Godot access.
Provides one guarded process adapter, default denial, dev allowlisting, and allow/deny audit records.
Validates security-sensitive signal names/arguments and integrates drift detection into CI checks.
Seeds combat with the Warrior starting deck through shared deck state rather than placeholder hands.
Creates, mutates, and visibly applies Warrior Rage through the shared combat runtime.
Binds generated ActConfig graphs to visible reachable, locked, selected, and completed map states.
Restores locked Reward/Shop/Event autosave surfaces while preserving deterministic offers and route ownership.
Executes relic effects through the shared combat trigger path after acquisition/display integration.
Promotes AOE and multi-hit rules into live combat using deterministic shared damage target order.
Aligns combat feedback surfaces with actual trigger, fixed-damage, and AOE resolution results.
Audits T70-T101 sizing and splits work exceeding one deterministic Chapter 6 closure.
Splits review validation of primary Continue boundaries from locked-surface restoration; it changes review scope.
Separates combat core rule integration review from scene feedback reconciliation.
Resolves the displayed enemy action once at player-turn end and enforces no-repeat rules.
Makes powers and relics visible, inspectable, and effectful through shared combat hooks.
Displays stored reward and relic settlement results without recomputing run state.
Separates enemy preview review from turn resolution and no-repeat verification.
Separates settlement owner-surface, reward/relic metadata, and resume-evidence review lanes.
Executes relic effects at shared run trigger boundaries outside direct combat resolution.
Makes potions visible, inspectable, and effectful through the shared combat trigger path.
Separates combat-trigger relic review from broader run-trigger closure review.
Displays stored resume evidence on settlement without mutating or recomputing run state.
Stabilizes Reward offer locking across re-entry and fails safely on invalid pool context.
Writes the confirmed card into the live deck, leaves it unchanged on skip, and resolves through the owned return route once.
Synchronizes enemy surfaces to data-backed runtime enemies and supplies visible invalid-definition fallback.

ambiguities.description: Chapter 7 rows reference an unavailable candidates file. Membership is based only on the named surfaces; detailed widgets, events, and closure requirements cannot be inferred.
Supersession is stated collectively by T123-T130. No exact predecessor-to-successor mapping or surviving settings/config-audit requirements is inferred.
This remains an accounted-for umbrella checkpoint over T80-T82, not a separately implementable deck system.
These rows govern sizing and review lanes. Gameplay subjects in their titles are review context, not authorization to implement additional runtime behavior.
Offer locking is described generically; no unsupported claim is made that every node consumes a particular implementation.

The row explicitly names relics, events, and other run-state systems as reward modifiers. Cross-listing relic integration reflects that scope; it does not define unsupplied event or modifier implementations.
Referenced ADRs, design gates, M1 content lists, migration backlogs, and project context were not supplied and were not consulted; only explicit row text was used.
Many view-specific cells contain replacement glyphs. Usable titles, design scopes, and readable details provide the grouping evidence; missing cell contents were not reconstructed.
The source projects task scope rather than authoritative task status. Active here means not explicitly superseded in this source, not pending or incomplete.

interpretation: Optional semantic reference/navigation groupings only. Membership is not task ordering, authority, acceptance, delivery status, or a new workflow.

selection.method: Three isolated same-model analyses with identical inputs and instructions; reviewer selected run 3 by source fidelity and boundary clarity.
